For a single, static map, the end result of this article is definitively better than the initial Google maps.

But Google maps is not consumed in printed, static form: it is always on a interactive device where you can scroll and zoom in and zoom out and search for a location and have the map show you where it is. In almost all situations, you can also ask it for directions from your current location to somewhere else or directions from one location to another.

Google's maps (and apple's, for that matter) are not meant to be glanced at and then ignored; they are an interactive product and when used that way, completely outperform traditional static maps.

A more interesting comparison, in my opinion, would be the maps that MapQuest produces versus traditional printed maps, as those generally are intended to be printed and consumed in a static fashion.
